editMechanics.conclusion: The delimiter does not decide whether the carry happens; it decides which files it happens in. TAB carries a tab on tab-indented files, PIPE carries a space on space-indented files, NONE has no delimiter to carry, and native's own Read has the TAB defect at the same rate.

[M] no ss-search/ss-find result block ever named a .jam file over 198 rollouts; 62 --in-scoped greps returned (no matches) on files that exist. 2 of 22 pool tasks (9%) have gold sweet-search cannot index; 2 more are part-blind.

levers.zeroCostFalsifier: re-index the two b2 goldens with .jam added and src/build/ un-excluded, then replay the exact ss-search / ss-grep queries recorded in the traces
levers.kill: src/tools/stage.jam still absent from the top-20 for the queries the agents actually wrote
levers.discardLogCheck: not in SLATE-A section 9 or SLATE-B section 8. SLATE-A 9.3 ('more sibling retrieval') is a ranking proposal; this is a corpus proposal — the file is absent from the index, not ranked low.

levers.name: Say 'not indexed', never (no matches)
levers.mechanism: [M] 69 single-invocation ss-* calls answered (no matches) for an --in scope the same rollout had already read successfully. bfgroup__b2-259/r0 burned 30 empty results in one rollout.
levers.change: in cmdGrep's scoped branch (_ss-helpers.mjs:324) and in cmdFind/cmdAgentSearch (:474, :771), print '(not indexed: <path> — use native grep)' when the scope exists on disk but contributes no indexed content
levers.zeroCostFalsifier: count how many of the 69 were followed within 3 calls by another ss-* call with the same scope
levers.kill: fewer than a third are followed by a retry — then the message would not change behaviour
levers.discardLogCheck: not a 'return the same information more compactly' move (SLATE-B section 8, banned) — it adds information the agent does not have. Not in either log.

levers.name: Accept a positional path as a scope in ss-grep; give ss-find --in
levers.mechanism: [M] 70 exit-2 usage errors in 33 of 198 rollouts. Dominant form is grep muscle memory 'ss-grep "<pat>" <path> -k N'; second is ss-find ... --in <path>, an option ss-grep has and ss-find does not ([C] FIND_USAGE).
levers.zeroCostFalsifier: re-parse the 70 rejected command lines with the proposed rule; count recoveries and check no currently-valid command changes meaning
levers.kill: fewer than 50 of 70 recover, or any currently-working call changes result
levers.discardLogCheck: not present. Not SLATE-A 9.12 free-argument call packing — no calls are merged; a rejected call becomes an executed one.

levers.name: Fail a bad regex before loading the models, and print the rg diagnostic
levers.mechanism: [M] 37 calls in 27 rollouts crash with a truncated 'rg: regex parse error:'; the same 37 calls carry BinaryHNSW/LateInteraction load chatter, because the crash happens on the cold fallback path after the models load ([C] _ss-helpers.mjs:343-347)
levers.zeroCostFalsifier: compile the 37 recorded patterns with the same regex engine; confirm all 37 fail at compile time before any index work
levers.kill: any of the 37 compiles cleanly — then the diagnosis is wrong
levers.discardLogCheck: not present. Related to the ss-grep BRE bug in project_cost_forensics_results, which is now fixed (dialect retry recovers 74 of 87); this is a different, unmitigated path.

levers.name: Give ss-read an unambiguous gutter on tab-indented files
levers.mechanism: [M] 8 of 14 locatable TAB anchor failures are exactly one tab too deep, all in the one tab-indented repo. Native's Read has the same defect (7 of 20).
levers.whyStillOpen: FRESH-POOL closed 'which of tab, pipe or none is best' (p >= 0.72). The open question is narrower and has a mechanism: a delimiter equal to the file's own indent character is ambiguous. A form unambiguous in BOTH families is not one of the three that were tested.
levers.scope: small — 13.9% of delivered ss-read lines are tab-indented; the failures cost calls, not rollouts (moq is dead for an unrelated reason)
levers.zeroCostFalsifier: re-render the 14 TAB and 9 PIPE failed anchors under the candidate delimiter and check the strip is unique
levers.kill: the candidate costs more than 0.93 tokens/line over tab (the whole delimiter budget), or the count of rollouts it would have saved is 0 — which on this evidence it is
levers.discardLogCheck: the delimiter A/B is superseded by FRESH-POOL-RESULTS.md section 5, which withdraws the per-harness recommendation. My evidence is new — no earlier pool had a tab-indented file — but the disposition stands: do NOT ship a delimiter change on resolution grounds. File as a rendering-correctness fix with a cost ceiling, or not at all.

levers.zeroCostFalsifier: grep the harness condenser path for the case where a summary is emitted with no following turn

levers.discardLogCheck: stop-discipline is a live class (project_mpp_stop_discipline_fix_tasks, project_engine_harness_fixes_p2_audit — condenser gates already shipped). Report it; run nothing for it.
